experiment: smPIFE (single-molecule protein-induced fluorescence enhancement) on SiMPull-immobilised protein, prism-type TIRF, 30 ms exposure, 1 min acquisition; sliding vs static traces, dwell-time analysis
buffer: 20 mM Tris pH7.5 and 25 mM NaCl imaging buffer with oxygen scavenging system (0.5% glucose, glucose-oxidase, catalase) and 2.5 mg/ml trolox; not phosphate
ligand_or_partner: 1 nM Cy3/DY547-labelled RNA: 25, 40, 55 bp dsRNA, pre-let7, TAR, tRNA-like RNA
construct_or_mutation: Full-length human TRBP with C-terminal EYFP (two dsRBD-I domains, 61 aa linker), overexpressed in A549 cells, pulled down from lysate with biotinylated anti-GFP antibody; isolated dsRBD1 is the entry construct
other_conditions: related structures: 3LLH (TRBP dsRBD1, used only for modelling). Measured on the RNA side because the protein is surface-anchored; PIFE sensitive under ~4 nm, intensity increase ~2-2.5-fold on protein approach. Temperature not stated. Sliding fraction per RNA from >300 traces; duration averaged over 50-100 sliding traces
dynamics_type: ATP-independent sliding/diffusion of dsRBP along dsRNA (translational, whole-protein/whole-duplex scale)
timescale: average continuous sliding time = 30-40 s for TRBP (average over 50-100 traces; likely underestimated due to photobleaching and 1 min acquisition); dwell time (peak-to-peak interval per sliding round) increases with duplex length 25/40/55 bp (per-trace analysis)
population: On average ~70% of RNA-bound TRBP molecules showed sliding on all RNA substrates except tRNA-like RNA (rest static)
author_claim: Full-length TRBP slides on both structured and non-structured dsRNA, more than Staufen1, ADAR1 and ADAD2, possibly because of the long flexible linker between its dsRBDs.
anchor: On average, 70% of TRBP showed sliding activity on all RNA substrates tested with the exception of tRNA, likely due to the limited length of dsRNA.
locator: Results, 'Dynamic property of dsRBP-dsRNA interaction' (Figure 4C-E); conditions: Methods, PIFE assay and Protein lysate preparation
caveat_note: This is the full-length EYFP-fused protein, not the isolated dsRBD1 of the entry, and the data cannot say whether dsRBD1 alone slides or how it contributes. The signal is intensity fluctuation of an RNA-attached dye. The length-dependent dwell time supports sliding, but the data do not give a structural state. Times are lower bounds, and the paper's own reference to HEK293 versus A549 expression is inconsistent. The 30-40 s figure is a duration of continuous sliding, not an exchange rate. No temperature is stated.

experiment: All-atom MD (NAMD2, AMBER force field with SB and BSC0 corrections) of TRBP dsRBD1 bound to a 35-bp RNA duplex; contact area and interaction energy
ligand_or_partner: 35-bp dsRNA duplex (built with 3DNA, placed on the 3ADL-based starting complex)
construct_or_mutation: Human TRBP dsRBD1 modelled from pdbID 3LLH
other_conditions: related structures: 3LLH, 3ADL. NpT, 1 bar, Langevin gamma = 1.0 ps-1, PME, 1.0 fs time step for the TRBP dsRBDs, 2 ns equilibration, 100 ns production; values averaged over last 85 ns after initial 15 ns relaxation. Experimental Kd values from cited work: dsRBD1 = 220 nM, dsRBD2 = 113 nM. Contact area and energy values are only in Figure 5C (仅图示). pH and buffer not stated
dynamics_type: binding energetics of dsRBD1-dsRNA interface (static contact area and interaction energy), no conformational exchange reported
timescale: simulation length = 100 ns; averaging window = last 85 ns after 15 ns relaxation (single trajectory per complex)
author_claim: TRBP dsRBD1 has a reduced contact area and interaction energy with dsRNA relative to TRBP dsRBD2, in line with its weaker experimental affinity.
anchor: TRBP–dsRBD1 and ADAR1–dsRBD3 have reduced affinities for dsRNA.
locator: Results, 'Sequence and structure analysis of dsRBD binding to dsRNA' (Figure 5C); conditions: Materials and Methods, Structural models of RNA constructs and dsRBDs
caveat_note: The MD reports averaged interaction energy and contact area, not intrinsic dynamics of dsRBD1 or sliding. A single 100 ns trajectory is far shorter than the sliding durations seen by smPIFE, so it neither shows nor excludes sliding or us-ms motion. Numeric contact areas and energies are shown only in a figure and are not given in the text. The result concerns the isolated domain bound to a 35-bp RNA rather than the free dsRBD1 of the entry.
